Merge bitcoin-core/gui#947: Update RPC console wallet when the active wallet changes

9ee30341032cdd414d6b74c9ebe97fb8daf1b320 gui: Update RPC console wallet when the active wallet changes (Kyle 🐆)

Pull request description:

  When multiple wallets are loaded, switching the active wallet via the main window's wallet selector doesn't update the wallet used by the RPC console. Console commands keep running against the previously selected wallet, so a wallet RPC can be sent to a different wallet than the one shown as active.

  The open/create/restore/migrate paths already call `RPCConsole::setCurrentWallet()`, but the main window selector was missed. Add the call to the central `setCurrentWallet()`.

  To reproduce: load two wallets, switch the active wallet in the toolbar, then run a wallet command such as `getwalletinfo` in the console.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36912: doc: relax clang-format loop and template declaration rules

fa07938a6f5c904aecf5d7925dbaf374a9db4897 doc: clang-format: AlwaysBreakTemplateDeclarations: No (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  I think it is clear that devs are not following the clang-format config here even in new code, and I don't want to rub this in during review, nor do I want to see clang-format edit those when I use it locally.

  So relax the config to allow those.

  References:

  https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangFormatStyleOptions.html#allowshortloopsonasingleline:

  ```
  git grep --line-number --perl-regexp '^\s*for \([^)]+\) [^{]+;$' ./src/ | wc -l
  -> 111
  ```

  https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangFormatStyleOptions.html#alwaysbreaktemplatedeclarations:

  ```
  git grep --line-number --perl-regexp '^\s*template\s*<.*>\s*(?:class|struct|[A-Za-z_])' | wc -l
  -> 162
  ```

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36040: Wallet: Don't backdate locktime rbf 596dd6fd88efe92133a34a0ba8d00f5f369a4bfd Test: bumpfee does not backdate the locktime (Biel) b1ddb7d6857668c82efefebe94f6ba224f71ab4a Wallet: Do not allow bumpfee to backdate the replacement transaction locktime (Biel) Pull request description: Closes https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/26526 Currently, in Bitcoin Core, given an original transaction A and its replacement B, we refer to **backdating** when the locktime of A is higher than the locktime of B (`A.locktime > B.locktime`). This can happen because Bitcoin Core enables **anti-fee-sniping** by default, which sets the transaction's locktime to the current block height. For privacy, 10% of the time, it instead sets a different locktime, randomly chosen between the current height and the current height minus 100 blocks. This can lead into having a replacement of a transaction with a locktime older than its original transaction. This is unrealistics and can be used as a wallet fingerprint. You can find a functional test to reproduce the behaviour mentioned [here](https://gist.github.com/Bicaru20/9afcb878dd103369255cd81cffac86ba) The approach proposed in this PR adds a new parameter to `CoinControl` to keep track of the previous locktime in the case of a `bumpfee`. We then pass this parameter to the DiscourageFeeSniping function through a new parameter, `minimum_height`, whose default value is set to 0.
Alternative approach: Since the locktime of the new transaction is 0, we also considered setting it to the previous locktime value and then, inside `DiscourageFeeSniping`, saving the previous locktime and setting the transaction's locktime to the block height before applying any of the backdating logic. This way, we could avoid passing a new parameter to the function. We ultimately decided not to go with this approach, as it makes the code more difficult to follow.
The only RPC that is affected by this changes is `bumpfee`. The pr also includes a functional test in `wallet_bumpfee.py` to test that when replacing a transation using `bumpfee` the locktime is not backdated.
We also conducted a small analysis to see how many the backdating in RBF transactions actually happen. We have data on the replaced transactions from 2025-05-01 to 2026-06-01. With that we have been able to detect this many backdatings: _We took the date of the last transaction of the replacement chain (A replacement chain are all the transactions that replace themselves)_ In total we have over 1,000,000 rbf transactions, but we see that on average there are only about 200-300 hundred replaccements backdating per week. Looking at the percentages we see that on average is less than 2% of all the transactions that have been replaced. So, it is clear that backdating in replacement transactions is unusual. However, the few transactions that do exhibit backdating are easily fingerprintable as having been replaced using `bumpfee` in Bitcoin Core or Electrum.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36342: wallet: reject recipient amounts above MAX_MONEY

bab579e56aa8b80a6f2923285e55cbcb2a7730b8 wallet: reject recipient amounts outside MoneyRange (Bruce0X)

Pull request description:

  `CreateTransaction` checks that recipient amounts aren't negative, but not that they're within `MAX_MONEY`. `CreateTransactionInternal` then sums them into `recipients_sum` (spend.cpp:1100) with no range check, and that sum can overflow.

  Easiest way to hit it is `fundrawtransaction` with a raw tx that has two outputs of 2^62 sat. It can also be reached with only valid amounts through `walletcreatefundedpsbt`/`send`/`sendmany` and a few thousand 21M BTC outputs. The "Transaction too large" check only runs after coin selection, so it doesn't stop this. On master the node aborts:

  ```
  Assertion failed: (!m_selected_inputs.empty()), function RecalculateWaste, file coinselection.cpp, line 904.
  ```

  UBSan reports the overflow at spend.cpp:1100 first. With other values the sum wraps to a small positive number instead, and `fundrawtransaction` returns success for a tx with outputs of 46116860184 BTC each.

  This checks every amount and the running sum against `MoneyRange` in the existing recipients loop of `CreateTransactionInternal`, before the amount is added to `recipients_sum`, and returns "Transaction output amount must be valid" before coin selection starts. The same check rejects negative amounts, so the separate negative check in `CreateTransaction` is removed. The new `test_outputs_above_max_money` in `wallet_fundrawtransaction.py` covers a single output above MAX_MONEY, two outputs whose sum is above it, a sum that overflows int64, and a negative output. On master the first case returns "Insufficient funds" and the overflow case crashes the node; with the fix all of them get the new error. `wallet_fundrawtransaction.py`, `wallet_send.py`, `wallet_basic.py` and `rpc_psbt.py` pass.

5a699cc2539856027d2a788b9604989d553b4d30 torcontrol: send -torpassword hex-encoded to avoid escaping bugs (jpk68)

Pull request description:

  The Tor password was sent as a `QuotedString` with only double quotes escaped; as Tor interprets backslash escapes inside it, any password containing a backslash was mangled (or left the string unterminated).

  The Tor Control spec deliberately allows the token to be sent as unquoted hex "to avoid escaping issues", as the `SAFECOOKIE` response already is. This patch does the same for the password, and also adds a functional test covering backslashes and quotes.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36501: refactor : Reorder CBlockIndex members to save 8 bytes

14edee63b643a96d7588897f0d00002228082178 Reorder CBlockIndex members to save 8 bytes (bartoli)

Pull request description:

  It seems we can save 8 bytes per CBlockIndex instance by reordering one class member. Moving one 8-byte field seems to avoid losing 2x 4 bytes to structure padding on a 64-bit build (on a 32-bit build, there is no gain).

  I could not exactly measure the runtime gain from just this (smaller than RAM usage variation between 2 launches), but I confirmed there was about as many instances of CBlockIndex as blocks in the chain (increasing CBlockIndex size by 320 bytes increases RAM usage by ~300MB), so saving 8 bytes per instance should save about 8MB of RAM at current block height.

  The gain is small, but it seems like it has no cost/risk, since that structure is not used for serialization, and just reordering here should have no side effects.

  I saw a few other types that could gain a few bytes in size by doing something similar (for example, CTxIn), but they have far fewer instances in memory to make the change worth it.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36087: util: Add and use AssertUnreachable

fa9a4ddbaf16d7fc8f8c336600674b3c7facca16 test: Add assert_falsy linter, And use AssertUnreachable (MarcoFalke)
fa20a5c7059c0d1cfd84a24e101d399f57771092 scripted-diff: Replace falsy assertions with AssertUnreachable (MarcoFalke)
fa6b4604e8c0cb48a13f8daa1ac61630114f35c2 test: Remove unused includes in util_tests.cpp (MarcoFalke)
fa1574cdaaeb8b0fad2eeb394a594a3534ee650c refactor: Use AssertUnreachable() and remove dead code (MarcoFalke)
fa81e4700a9495b7216580da151f36674b5affde util: Add AssertUnreachable (MarcoFalke)
fa1c93477e6ac332219af3eb4c6a5fcc9434105d refactor: Replace unreachable run-time assert with compile time assert (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  The current code uses assertions with falsy literal values in a few places. This is perfectly fine, but this comes with a bit of confusion sometimes:

  * `assert(false)` may cause confusion when it is unclear if `NDEBUG` can disable it. (The intention is to disallow `NDEBUG` compilation). Also, it can lead to warnings when used with clang-cl.exe (GCC seems to understand it)
  * `Assert(false)` hides the noreturn attribute behind a function call, which may cause GCC return-type warnings. (Clang seems to understand it)

  See https://godbolt.org/z/h7PT3jh3Y for the clang-cl/GCC warning reproducer.

  * When C++23 will be allowed, devs may prefer `std::unreachable`. However, this is unsafe and will invoke UB.
  * There is confusion why a `CHECK_NONFATAL` macro exists, but no fatal equivalent.

  Fix all those issues by:

  * Adding a new `AssertUnreachable`, which directly calls the noreturn `internal_abort_helper` helper.
  * Adding an `assert_falsy` linter to enforce code to use this macro.

Pull request description:

  The current code uses assertions with falsy literal values in a few places. This is perfectly fine, but this comes with a bit of confusion sometimes:

  * `assert(false)` may cause confusion when it is unclear if `NDEBUG` can disable it. (The intention is to disallow `NDEBUG` compilation). Also, it can lead to warnings when used with clang-cl.exe (GCC seems to understand it)
  * `Assert(false)` hides the noreturn attribute behind a function call, which may cause GCC return-type warnings. (Clang seems to understand it)

  See https://godbolt.org/z/h7PT3jh3Y for the clang-cl/GCC warning reproducer.

  * When C++23 will be allowed, devs may prefer `std::unreachable`. However, this is unsafe and will invoke UB.
  * There is confusion why a `CHECK_NONFATAL` macro exists, but no fatal equivalent.

  Fix all those issues by:

  * Adding a new `AssertUnreachable`, which directly calls the noreturn `internal_abort_helper` helper.
  * Adding an `assert_falsy` linter to enforce code to use this macro.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36889: cmake: Switch `include_directories` -> `target_include_directories`

435d5b227748a0ac5d6d2887050acf02304576f2 cmake: Remove `WarnAboutGlobalProperties` module (Hennadii Stepanov)
460f877fac200ccfde265d12613b352def903cf0 cmake: Switch `include_directories` -> `target_include_directories` (Hennadii Stepanov)
4ef05d6f45620254417fe6be701bebbf1a42619a cmake: Link `bitcoin_ipc` against `core_interface` (Hennadii Stepanov)

Pull request description:

  Use of non-target directives is not recommended. As of CMake 4.5.0, such use triggers `-Wnon-target-directive` warnings:
  ```console
  $ cmake -B build -Wnon-target-directive
  <snip>
  CMake Warning (non-target-directive) at src/CMakeLists.txt:8 (include_directories):
    Use of non-target directives is not recommended.  Consider
    target_include_directories instead.
  This warning is for project developers.  Use -Wno-author or
  -Wno-non-target-directive to suppress it.

  <snip>
  ```

  This PR:
  1. Links `bitcoin_ipc` against `core_interface`, so that `ipc/stub.cpp` is compiled with the project-wide build flags.

  2. Replaces the `include_directories()` call in `src/CMakeLists.txt` with `target_include_directories()`.

  3. Removes the custom [`WarnAboutGlobalProperties`](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/29f7e30d547c30ddb7a637bc3a2dbc7c0e3f5469/cmake/module/WarnAboutGlobalProperties.cmake) module, which is superseded by the new CMake warning.

  ---

  The counterpart for the `secp256k1` repo is https://github.com/bitcoin-core/secp256k1/pull/1996.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36894: net_processing: set fDisconnect instead of calling DisconnectNode

d63068c58ec9fcc94876bce30865d1a7266d64d4 net_processing: set fDisconnect instead of calling DisconnectNode (Eugene Siegel)

Pull request description:

  `MaybeDiscourageAndDisconnect` calls `DisconnectNode` which creates a `CSubNet` containing only the `CNode`'s address. This will disconnect every `CNode` with the same IP address. This is normally not a problem, except for clearnet-over-tor. If a node has an honest clearnet-over-tor inbound connection, the IP of the inbound peer will be the exit node's IP address. If an attacker connects to the node through the same exit node and sends an invalid message, they can cause every inbound peer sharing the exit node's IP to get disconnected. Fix this by only disconnecting the misbehaving `CNode` rather than every `CNode` sharing the IP.

commit.message:
net_processing: set fDisconnect instead of calling DisconnectNode

MaybeDiscourageAndDisconnect calls DisconnectNode which creates a
CSubNet containing only the CNode's address. This will disconnect
every CNode with the same IP address. This is normally not a problem,
except for clearnet-over-tor. If a node has an honest clearnet-over-tor
inbound connection, the IP of the inbound peer will be the exit node's
IP address. If an attacker connects to the node through the same exit
node and sends an invalid message, they can cause every inbound peer
sharing the exit node's IP to get disconnect. Fix this by only
disconnecting the misbehaving CNode rather than every CNode sharing
the IP.

commit.message:
scripted-diff: Replace falsy assertions with AssertUnreachable

Replace assertions with falsy literal values by the explicit
unreachable-code assertion macro.

-BEGIN VERIFY SCRIPT-

 # Paths to edit.
 # Excluded are subtrees and modules that can not include util/check.
 paths=(
   'src'
   ':(exclude)src/script/interpreter.cpp'
   ':(exclude)src/tinyformat.h'
   ':(exclude)src/univalue/'
   ':(exclude)src/crc32c'
   ':(exclude)src/crypto/ctaes'
   ':(exclude)src/ipc/libmultiprocess'
   ':(exclude)src/leveldb'
   ':(exclude)src/minisketch'
   ':(exclude)src/secp256k1'
 )

 for f in $(git grep -l --extended-regexp '\<(a|A)ssert\((0|false)\)' -- "${paths[@]}"); do

   # Add the util/check.h includes
   if ! grep --quiet "util/check.h" "$f"; then
     line=$(grep --line-number --max-count=1 '^#include' "$f" | cut --delimiter=: --fields=1)
     sed --in-place "${line}i#include <util/check.h>" "$f"
   fi

   # Remove cassert includes
   sed --in-place '/^#include <cassert>$/d' "$f"

   # Sort includes
   git diff -U1 $f | ./contrib/devtools/clang-format-diff.py -p1 -i -v

   # Use AssertUnreachable
   sed --in-place --regexp-extended 's/\<(a|A)ssert\((0|false)\)/AssertUnreachable()/g' "$f"

 done

-END VERIFY SCRIPT-

commit.message:
memusage: Make fields of STL helper structs public

The `stl_tree_node`, `list_node` and `unordered_node` class templates
only mimic the layout of the standard library's container nodes, so
that `sizeof` yields an estimate of the memory they use. Their fields
are never accessed.

Since llvm/llvm-project#237374, Clang 24 diagnoses these fields with
`-Wunused-private-field`.

This change drops the `private:` access specifiers. It does not affect
the size or alignment of the structs, as all their fields keep the same
access control, and it is consistent with `stl_shared_counter`.

050409b2c5522eff0dc37c00a6d1225a8a437e17 test: allow 3 bytes of fee overestimate in assert_fee_amount (Ferdinando Ametrano)

Pull request description:

  The wallet sizes a transaction assuming a 71-byte low-R ECDSA signature. A signature whose r or s has leading zero bytes is shorter, so the fee can cover a few bytes more than the signed transaction needs. In #36394 the wallet estimated 219 bytes and paid 438 sat at 2 sat/vB, but the signed transaction was 216 bytes: the signature was 3 bytes short.   I raise the allowance to 3 bytes, which makes the failure about 200 times rarer. The check that the fee is not too low is unchanged. maflcko suggested 3 bytes in #24151 and #25164.

  Fixes #36394.

commit.message:
fuzz: reuse one fuzzed wallet across inputs

FuzzedWallet was rebuilt for every input. That imports eight
descriptors, and each address it then hands out costs a BIP32
derivation plus three separate WalletBatch transactions (see
DescriptorScriptPubKeyMan::GetNewDestination) - all paid before the
target reaches the code under test.

Build the wallet once in the target's .init hook and reset it per
input instead.

wallet: add test-only helper to clear in-memory transaction state

Add CWallet::ClearInMemoryTxStateForTest(), which drops mapWallet,
wtxOrdered, mapTxSpends, m_txos and m_locked_coins, leaving the
database, the wallet flags and the ScriptPubKeyMans untouched.

This exists so that fuzz harnesses can reuse a single wallet across
inputs instead of rebuilding it for every one. m_txos and mapTxSpends
are private, so a harness cannot reset them on its own.

RemoveTxs() is not usable here: it erases each transaction's
m_it_wtxOrdered from wtxOrdered, and that iterator is only valid for
transactions added through AddToWallet(). Harnesses that populate
mapWallet directly leave it uninitialized.

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36556: depends: fix non-atomic reads in capnp debug assertions

6e8e85ddcf2eb4a062fab3cd2b9c046edfbf72ec depends: fix non-atomic reads in capnp debug assertions (xyzconstant)

Pull request description:

  KJ's debug assertions read the mutex futex word and `AtomicRefcounted` refcounts non-atomically. The TSan job builds capnp without optimization, which automatically enables these assertions, and TSan reports these reads as data races the moment KJ objects start communicating across threads.

  libmultiprocess enables cross-thread communication for the first time in bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#376, which replaces the pipe used in `EventLoop::sync()` with `kj::Executor::executeSync()`. This is what triggered the [failure](https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/actions/runs/38094008438/job/114336046070?pr=376).

  Patches are the upstream commits capnproto/capnproto@b91a6ba7c7 and capnproto/capnproto@cc13c8c45f, which are backports of the v2 fixes in capnproto/capnproto#2781 and capnproto/capnproto#2843 (backport PR: capnproto/capnproto#2855).
